title: Generation of a module derived category by shifts of the ring
statement: For a ring $A$, let $D(A)$ be the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian category of $A$-modules. Every object $K$ of $D(A)$ belongs to the smallest full subcategory of $D(A)$ that contains all shifts $A[k]$, $k\in\mathbf Z$, and is closed under set-indexed direct sums, under the third vertex of a distinguished triangle whose other two vertices lie in it, and under retracts.

source.place: More on Algebra, Remark 15.60.11 (more-algebra-remark-P-resolution), Tag 09PB, as invoked in perfect.tex Lemma 36.22.1 (Tag 08EU)

proof.text: Represent $K$ by a cochain complex $M^\bullet$ of $A$-modules. Apply [lem-pc-derived-filtered-free-resolution] to obtain a quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to M^\bullet$ and a filtration $F_iP^\bullet$ whose successive quotients are direct sums of shifts of $A$ and whose inclusions are termwise split.

source.place: Differential Graded Algebra, Lemma 15.60.9 (Tag 09KP), specialized to ordinary rings

proof.text: Each quotient triangle $F_iP^\bullet\to F_{i+1}P^\bullet\to F_{i+1}P^\bullet/F_iP^\bullet\to F_iP^\bullet[1]$ and induction on $i$ show that every $F_iP^\bullet$ belongs to the full subcategory generated by the shifts $A[k]$ under direct sums and the third vertex of distinguished triangles: the quotient is a direct sum of shifts as a complex, and by [lem-pc-derived-module-direct-sums] this termwise direct sum is the direct sum of those shifts in $D(A)$, and the zero initial term is in the subcategory.

source.place: More on Algebra, Remark 15.60.11 (Tag 09PB), filtration argument

proof.text: The filtration gives a short exact sequence of complexes $0\to\bigoplus_iF_iP^\bullet\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\bigoplus_iF_iP^\bullet\to P^\bullet\to0$: the map is injective by inspecting the least nonzero summand, and its cokernel is the filtered union $\bigcup_iF_iP^\bullet=P^\bullet$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] this yields the mapping-telescope distinguished triangle $\bigoplus_iF_iP^\bullet\to\bigoplus_iF_iP^\bullet\to P^\bullet\to(\bigoplus_iF_iP^\bullet)[1]$. By [lem-pc-derived-module-direct-sums] the termwise direct sum $\bigoplus_iF_iP^\bullet$ is the direct sum of the $F_iP^\bullet$ in $D(A)$; since the first two vertices are these direct sums, closure under set-indexed direct sums and distinguished triangles puts $P^\bullet$ in the generated subcategory.

source.place: More on Algebra, Remark 15.60.11 (Tag 09PB), displayed telescope triangle

proof.text: The quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to M^\bullet$ becomes an isomorphism in $D(A)$, so $K$ is isomorphic to an object in the generated full subcategory and hence belongs to it. Allowing retracts only enlarges this subcategory, which proves the stated claim.

proof_origin.place: Reconstructed from More on Algebra, Remark 15.60.11 (Tag 09PB)

statement_change.old_statement: For a ring $A$, every object $K$ of $D(A)$ [def-pc-derived-category] belongs to the smallest full subcategory of $D(A)$ that contains all shifts $A[k]$, $k\in\mathbf Z$, and is closed under set-indexed direct sums, under the third vertex of a distinguished triangle whose other two vertices lie in it, and under retracts.
statement_change.what: The cited dependency def-pc-derived-category defines D(O_X) for a scheme X, so it does not introduce D(A) for a ring A; the original statement therefore had an undefined and mismatched derived category. The corrected statement follows the source and cites the general derived category of an abelian category.
